title: T12 tells the reader on G2 that every representation of the board 'needs more than the game', which SPEC 2.18 and M8 beat 7 contradict
location: site/src/components/tools/t12/rep.ts:441-444 (noMinusculeSentence, data-out="no-minuscule"); shown on every node of G2 at /tools/rep/
claim: On G2, F4 and E8, T12 prints 'This board has no minuscule node; its representations need more than the game.' For G2 this is false by the specification. SPEC 2.18's other recipe, 'One zero weight', builds the 7-dimensional representation of G2 from the game ([V]). The code cites SPEC 2.18 [D], but that [D] covers only the representations out of reach of both recipes.
expected: SPEC 2.18 'One zero weight': 'the 7-dimensional representation of G2 ... The Chevalley-Serre relations hold [V for A1, B2, B3, B4 and G2]. This gives the site a route to G2 that stays inside the game'. 'Out of reach of these two recipes: every other representation ... says plainly that the matrices need more than the game [D]'. M8 beat 7 on the same lesson: 'the 7-dimensional representation of G2. A later version of this module builds them from single steps as well.' On G2 the sentence should say that the minuscule recipe builds none of its representations, without claiming every representation needs more than the game.
observed: /tools/rep/?z=1&g=G2&k=1 and k=2, hydrated, data-out="no-minuscule": 'This board has no minuscule node; its representations need more than the game.' noMinusculeSentence(buildRepresentation(G2, 1)) returns the same string. title: T12's signed-move panel states the minuscule identities on every built node, where they are false (D4 node 2, the acceptance example) or their stated failure is false (B3 node 1)
location: site/src/components/tools/T12RepresentationBuilder.svelte:918-934 (snippet signedPanel; the panel is drawn whenever rep.built, line 1087); route /tools/rep/?z=1&g=D4&k=2. M8's challenge b10 sends the reader to E6 node 2, where the same false text shows.
claim: The panel prints, with no condition, 'Firing node k permutes the positions: its matrix is Ek + Fk + Pk ... The group element exp(Ek) exp(−Fk) exp(Ek) is Ek − Fk + Pk: the same matrix with one sign changed in each pair.' On every node that is not minuscule it adds 'the moves of numbers 2 or more are missing from E and F, so the signed matrix is no longer the move with signs.' The first two sentences are false wherever the orbit has a number of size 2 or more at node k. The third is false wherever it has none.
expected: SPEC 2.18 states both identities 'in a minuscule representation', and verify.py section 14 checks them on the 18 minuscule records only. On D4 node 2 at k = 2, the firing matrix S_2 is a permutation, but E2+F2+P2^0 has zero columns at ±alpha_2. Likewise (I+E2)(I−F2)(I+E2) = exp(E2)exp(−F2)exp(E2) is invertible, but E2−F2+P2^0 is singular. On B3 node 1 at k = 1, every number at node 1 is −1, 0 or 1, so S_1 = E1+F1+P1^0 and the signed matrix is the move with signs.
observed: D4 node 2: the panel text as quoted, beside 'Signed: E2 − F2 + P2' with empty columns at (1,−2,1,1) and (−1,2,−1,−1). B3 node 1: the panel says 'no longer the move with signs', but the engine's matrices satisfy both identities at node 1. Oracle over the 509 (node, k) states of the 85 built non-minuscule nodes: the first two sentences are false in 450 states and the third in the other 59 (B_n node 1, C_n node n, B2 node 1 at k = node).

specRef: SPEC.md 2.18 'Minuscule representations: the game graph is the representation' ('So in a minuscule representation a game move is a Lie group element with its signs removed'); 4 T12 ('the move matrix beside its signed version'); reference/verify.py section 14 (checks only MINU); RED-TEAM-COMMON 4 (a mathematical statement presented as fact that is wrong).

title: T12's 'Dimension:' readout shows the size of the orbit on nodes that are not minuscule: 24 for node 2 of D4 (golden 28), 240 for node 8 of E8 (248), and 2160 on E8's default node 1 (3875)

The wrong values are pinned by site/tests/e2e/T12.spec.ts:138, 308, 318 and site/tests/unit/tools/T12.test.ts:1279.
claim: Beside 'Board X, node i', T12 prints 'Dimension: N' with N the number of positions in the orbit of omega_i. On a node that is not minuscule this is not the dimension of the representation of that node, and on an unbuilt node there are no matrices at all. The site therefore contradicts golden data and its own lesson.
expected: golden weyl_dimension gives 28 for D4 omega_2, 7 for G2 omega_1, 26 for F4 omega_4, 52 for F4 omega_1, 248 for E8 omega_8, 3875 for E8 omega_1 and 7 for B3 omega_1. M8 beat 6 prints 248 for E8 and 26 for F4, and T5's dimension calculator reproduces 3875. Otherwise the readout should not be called a dimension: the caption already says 'N by N matrices read off the game'.
observed: T12 shows 24, 6, 24, 24, 240, 2160 and 6 for those nodes. E8 and F4 open on node 1 by default, so their default states read 'Dimension: 2160' and 'Dimension: 24'. Over all 85 built nodes that are not minuscule, the readout differs from weyl_dimension in 85.
reproduction: From a clean checkout of 006f50d plus the reproducer: npm ci --prefer-offline; TMPDIR=<fresh dir> npx vitest run --project site-unit site/tests/unit/redteam-RT-09-p5-t12-claims.test.ts -t 'P5-RT-09-02' (7 tests fail: 'expected 24 to be 28', '6 to be 7', '24 to be 26', '240 to be 248', '6 to be 7', '2160 to be 3875', '24 to be 52').
